2609.09054.title: Training-Free Task Vectors for LLM Behavioral Control
2609.09054.paper_summary: Task vectors enable post-training model editing by identifying semantically meaningful directions in weight space, typically computed as the difference between a fine-tuned model and its pretrained initialization. However, this reliance on fine-tuning makes discovering such directions costly and limits the practicality of post-training model editing. To address this limitation, we introduce Training-Free Task Vectors (TFTVs), a novel method to compute task-vector-like directions without requiring fine-tuning. Our method maps activation steering vectors to rank-one weight-space edits using only forward-pass statistics, while satisfying arithmetic properties that directly support learning via addition, forgetting via subtraction, and the composition of multiple edits. Empirically, we evaluate TFTVs on large language model behavioral control tasks and show that they consistently amplify, suppress, and compose target behaviors while preserving general knowledge and problem-solving skills. We also validate our method against other editing and steering baselines, experimentally demonstrating that TFTVs achieve stronger trait control with better or competitive utility preservation. We hope our work opens new directions for the community in post-training model editing and broader training-free model control. Code is available on the project website: tftv-llm.github.io.
2609.09054.paper_summary_zh: 任務向量通過識別權重空間中具有語義意義的方向，使後訓練模型編輯成為可能，通常計算為微調模型與其預訓練初始化之間的差異。<lb/>然而，這種對微調的依賴使得發現這些方向的成本高昂，並限制了後訓練模型編輯的實用性。<lb/>為了解決這一限制，我們引入了無需訓練的任務向量（TFTVs），這是一種新穎的方法，可以計算類似任務向量的方向，而無需微調。<lb/>我們的方法僅使用前向傳遞統計，將激活引導向量映射到秩一權重空間編輯，同時滿足直接支持通過加法學習、通過減法遺忘和多次編輯組合的算術性質。<lb/>在實證上，我們在大型語言模型行為控制任務上評估了TFTVs，並顯示它們始終能夠放大、抑制和組合目標行為，同時保留一般知識和解決問題的技能。<lb/>我們還將我們的方法與其他編輯和引導基準進行了驗證，實驗性地證明TFTVs在特徵控制方面達到了更強的效果，並保持了更好或具競爭力的效用保存。<lb/>我們希望我們的工作為社區在後訓練模型編輯和更廣泛的無訓練模型控制方面開辟新的方向。<lb/>代碼可在項目網站上獲得：tftv-llm.github.io。
